newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower on dollar short-covering.

text.p: SEOUL, April 18 (Retuer) - The won closed lower on Friday on dollar short-covering, and dealers forecast tight-range trading would dominate the won/dollar market next week.
"Some shorts had no choice but to buy back the dollars to cover their positions after the dollar's fall was not enough," said a Commercial Bank of Korea.
The won closed at 894.10, compared with 893.70.

The dollar's strength against the yen in world markets and looming importer deals pushed the won opening lower at 894.50. But it rebounded to 893.10 on corporate dollar selling to reduce foreign currency reserves, dealers said.
Dealers said an expected dollar inflow for investments in the Seoul stock market would boost the local currency.
They forecast the central bank might step into the market to raise foreign reserves next month, when the foreign stockholding limit will be raised to 23 percent from current 20 percent.
"We cannot either go long amid falling dollars or short for fears of the intervention," said a foreign bank dealer. He expected the dollar to move at 890.00-895.00 won next week.
Monday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 893.70 against 893.40 today.
